# Part I

## Illustrative Example 1

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Gradient Boosting animation (sequential learning)
# ============================================================

library(ggplot2)
library(rpart)
library(gganimate)
library(gifski)
library(transformr)
library(dplyr)

set.seed(4050)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. True function
# ------------------------------------------------------------
truth_fun <- function(x) {
  ifelse(
    x < 2,
    0.8*sin(2*x),
    -0.8 + 0.4*sin(5*x)
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Simulate data
# ------------------------------------------------------------
n <- 250
x <- runif(n, 0, 4.5)
y <- truth_fun(x) + rnorm(n, sd = 0.35)

df <- data.frame(x, y)

grid <- data.frame(
  x = seq(min(df$x), max(df$x), length.out = 400)
)

truth_df <- data.frame(
  x = grid$x,
  y = truth_fun(grid$x)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Gradient Boosting loop
# ------------------------------------------------------------
M <- 100          # number of boosting iterations
lr <- 0.1        # learning rate

# initialize model (constant)
f_hat <- rep(mean(df$y), nrow(df))
f_hat_grid <- rep(mean(df$y), nrow(grid))

# store predictions over time
boost_mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(grid), ncol = M)

# store individual learners (for visualization)
tree_list <- vector("list", M)

for (m in 1:M) {

  # compute residuals
  residuals <- df$y - f_hat

  # fit weak learner
  tree <- rpart(
    residuals ~ x,
    data = df,
    control = rpart.control(
      cp = 0.001,
      maxdepth = 2   # shallow trees = classic boosting
    )
  )

  tree_list[[m]] <- tree

  # predictions
  pred_train <- predict(tree, newdata = df)
  pred_grid  <- predict(tree, newdata = grid)

  # update model
  f_hat <- f_hat + lr * pred_train
  f_hat_grid <- f_hat_grid + lr * pred_grid

  boost_mat[, m] <- f_hat_grid
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Build animation data (ensemble prediction)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
boost_df <- data.frame(
  x = rep(grid$x, M),
  yhat = as.vector(boost_mat),
  frame = rep(1:M, each = nrow(grid))
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Build data for current tree (residual learner)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
tree_df <- data.frame()

for (m in 1:M) {

  pred <- predict(tree_list[[m]], newdata = grid)

  tmp <- data.frame(
    x = grid$x,
    yhat = pred,
    frame = m
  )

  tree_df <- rbind(tree_df, tmp)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Plot + animation
# ------------------------------------------------------------
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, colour = "grey50") +

  # true function
  geom_line(
    data = truth_df,
    aes(x, y),
    colour = "blue",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +

  # current weak learner (residual fit)
  geom_step(
    data = tree_df,
    aes(x, yhat),
    colour = "black",
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +

  # boosted model
  geom_line(
    data = boost_df,
    aes(x, yhat),
    colour = "red",
    linewidth = 1.4
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Gradient Boosting (Sequential Learning)",
    subtitle = "Iteration: {closest_state}",
    y = "Response"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +

  transition_states(frame) +
  ease_aes("linear")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Render animation
# ------------------------------------------------------------
animate(
  p,
  fps = 5,
  width = 800,
  height = 500,
  renderer = gifski_renderer()
)
```

## Illustrative Example 2

```{r}

library(gbm)
library(rsample)
library(caret)

set.seed(4050)

iris_split <- initial_split(iris, prop = 0.75) 

# Extract the training and testing data frames
iris_train <- training(iris_split)
iris_test <- testing(iris_split)



model.gbm1 <- gbm(
  formula = Petal.Length ~.,
  data = iris_train,
  distribution = "gaussian",  # SSE loss function
  n.trees = 5000,
  shrinkage = 0.1,
  interaction.depth = 3,
  n.minobsinnode = 10,
  cv.folds = 10
)


best <- which.min(model.gbm1$cv.error) # Get best number of trees
best

sqrt(model.gbm1$cv.error[best]) # compute RMSE

# Plot
gbm.perf(model.gbm1, method = "cv")

# Testing set

postResample(predict(model.gbm1,iris_test), iris_test$Petal.Length)

```

## Example 1 from slides

```{r}

library(caret)
library(rsample)
library(dplyr)

set.seed(4050)

Wages <- read.csv("Wages.csv")

# 1 Perform a 75/25 train/test split.

Wages <- Wages[,2:12] 
  
Wages <- Wages %>% # Fixed
  mutate_if(is.character, as.factor)

W_split <- initial_split(Wages, prop = 0.75) 

# Extract the training and testing data frames
W_train <- training(W_split)
W_test <- testing(W_split)

# 2 Adjust the code from Illustrative Example 1 to construct a GBM model
# with Salary as the response variable (ignore the ID column).

model.gbmE1 <- gbm(
  formula = Salary ~ .,
  data = W_train,
  distribution = "gaussian",  # SSE loss function
  n.trees = 5000,
  shrinkage = 0.1,
  interaction.depth = 3,
  n.minobsinnode = 10,
  cv.folds = 10
)


# 3 What is the optimal number of trees?

best <- which.min(model.gbmE1$cv.error) # Get best number of trees
best

sqrt(model.gbmE1$cv.error[best]) # compute RMSE

# 4 Plot the progression of the number of trees.

gbm.perf(model.gbmE1, method = "cv")


# 5 Does our model predict the test set well?

postResample(predict(model.gbmE1,W_test), W_test$Salary)
```

## Illustrative Example 3 A

```{r}

# create grid search
hyper_grid <- expand.grid(
  learning_rate = c(0.3, 0.1, 0.05, 0.01, 0.005),
  RMSE = NA,
  trees = NA,
  time = NA
)

# execute grid search
for(i in seq_len(nrow(hyper_grid))) {

  # fit gbm
  set.seed(4050)  # for reproducibility
  train_time <- system.time({
    m <- gbm(
      formula = Petal.Length ~ .,
      data = iris_train,
      distribution = "gaussian",
      n.trees = 5000, 
      shrinkage = hyper_grid$learning_rate[i], 
      interaction.depth = 3, 
      n.minobsinnode = 10,
      cv.folds = 10 
   )
  })
  
  # add SSE, trees, and training time to results
  hyper_grid$RMSE[i]  <- sqrt(min(m$cv.error))
  hyper_grid$trees[i] <- which.min(m$cv.error)
  hyper_grid$Time[i]  <- train_time[["elapsed"]]

}

# results
arrange(hyper_grid, RMSE)


```

## Illustrative Example 3 B

```{r}
hyper_grid <- expand.grid(
  n.trees = 6000,
  shrinkage = 0.010,
  interaction.depth = c(1, 3, 5, 7),
  n.minobsinnode = c(3, 5, 10, 15)
)

# create model fit function
model_fit <- function(n.trees, shrinkage, interaction.depth, n.minobsinnode) {
  set.seed(123)
  m <- gbm(
    formula = Petal.Length ~ .,
      data = iris_train,
    distribution = "gaussian",
    n.trees = n.trees,
    shrinkage = shrinkage,
    interaction.depth = interaction.depth,
    n.minobsinnode = n.minobsinnode,
    cv.folds = 10
  )
  # compute RMSE
  sqrt(min(m$cv.error))
}

# perform search grid with functional programming
hyper_grid$rmse <- purrr::pmap_dbl(
  hyper_grid,
  ~ model_fit(
    n.trees = ..1,
    shrinkage = ..2,
    interaction.depth = ..3,
    n.minobsinnode = ..4
    )
)

# results
arrange(hyper_grid, rmse)


# Generalize?

model.gbm2 <- gbm(
  formula = Petal.Length ~.,
  data = iris_train,
  distribution = "gaussian",  # SSE loss function
  n.trees = 6000,
  shrinkage = 0.01,
  interaction.depth = 5,
  n.minobsinnode = 3,
  cv.folds = 10
)

postResample(predict(model.gbm1,iris_test), iris_test$Petal.Length)
postResample(predict(model.gbm2,iris_test), iris_test$Petal.Length)
```

# Part II

## Illustrative Example 1

```{r}

library(h2o)

set.seed(4050)

h2o.no_progress()  # turn off progress bars for brevity
h2o.init(max_mem_size = "5g")

# convert data to h2o object
data.h2o <- as.h2o(iris)

# Identify predictors and response 
response <- "Petal.Length"
predictors <- setdiff(names(data.h2o), response)

# Train and test split
splits <- h2o.splitFrame(data.h2o, ratios = 0.75, seed = 4050)

train_h2o <- splits[[1]]
test_h2o  <- splits[[2]]


# refined hyperparameter grid
hyper_grid <- list(
  sample_rate = c(0.5, 0.75, 1),              # row subsampling
  col_sample_rate = c(0.5, 0.75, 1),          # col subsampling for each split
  col_sample_rate_per_tree = c(0.5, 0.75, 1)  # col subsampling for each tree
)

# random grid search strategy
search_criteria <- list(
  strategy = "RandomDiscrete",
  stopping_metric = "mse",
  stopping_tolerance = 0.001,   
  stopping_rounds = 10,         
  max_runtime_secs = 60*60      
)

# perform grid search 
grid <- h2o.grid(
  algorithm = "gbm",
  grid_id = "gbm_grid",
  x = predictors, 
  y = response,
  training_frame = train_h2o,
  hyper_params = hyper_grid,
  ntrees = 6000,
  learn_rate = 0.01, # previous model
  max_depth = 5, # previous model
  min_rows = 3, # previous model
  nfolds = 10,
  stopping_rounds = 10,
  stopping_tolerance = 0,
  search_criteria = search_criteria,
  seed = 4050
)

# collect the results and sort by our model performance metric of choice
grid_perf <- h2o.getGrid(
  grid_id = "gbm_grid", 
  sort_by = "mse", 
  decreasing = FALSE
)

grid_perf


# Save the best model 
best_model <- h2o.getModel(grid_perf@model_ids[[1]])

# Performance metrics (C-V)
h2o.performance(model = best_model, xval = TRUE)

# Predictions 
predictions <- h2o.predict(object = best_model, newdata = test_h2o)


# Evaluate
postResample(as.vector(predictions),as.vector(test_h2o$Petal.Length))
```

## Illustrative Example 2

```{r}

library(xgboost)
library(recipes)


# Process data
xgb_prep <- recipe(Petal.Length ~ ., data = iris_train) %>%
  step_integer(all_nominal()) %>%
  prep(training = iris_train, retain = TRUE) %>%
  juice()

X <- as.matrix(xgb_prep[setdiff(names(xgb_prep), "Petal.Length")])
Y <- xgb_prep$Petal.Length

# Convert to DMatrix
dtrain <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X, label = Y)


# Use hyperparameters that we already found I.E.1

set.seed(4050)
iris_xgb <- xgb.cv(
  data = dtrain,
  nrounds = 6000,
  early_stopping_rounds = 50, 
  nfold = 10,
  params = list(
    objective = "reg:squarederror",
    eta = 0.01, # from I.E. 1
    max_depth = 5, # from I.E. 1
    min_child_weight = 3, # from I.E. 1
    subsample = 0.75, # from I.E. 1
    colsample_bytree = 1.0, # from I.E. 1
    colsample_bylevel = 0.5), # from I.E. 1
  verbose = 0
)  

# minimum test CV RMSE
min(iris_xgb$evaluation_log$test_rmse_mean)



#### 2 #####

# hyperparameter grid
hyper_grid <- expand.grid(
    eta = 0.01, # from I.E. 1
    max_depth = 5, # from I.E. 1
    min_child_weight = 3, # from I.E. 1
    subsample = 0.75, # from I.E. 1
    colsample_bytree = 1.0, # from I.E. 1
    colsample_bylevel = 0.5, # from I.E. 1
  gamma = c(0, 1, 10, 100),
  lambda = c(0, 0.1, 20),
  alpha = c(0, 0.1, 20),
  rmse = 0,          # a place to put RMSE results
  trees = 0          # a place to put required number of trees
)

# grid search
for(i in seq_len(nrow(hyper_grid))) {
  set.seed(4050)
  m <- xgb.cv(
  data = dtrain,
    nrounds = 4000,
    early_stopping_rounds = 50, 
    nfold = 10,
    verbose = 0,
    params = list( 
      objective = "reg:squarederror",
      eta = hyper_grid$eta[i], 
      max_depth = hyper_grid$max_depth[i],
      min_child_weight = hyper_grid$min_child_weight[i],
      subsample = hyper_grid$subsample[i],
      colsample_bytree = hyper_grid$colsample_bytree[i],
      gamma = hyper_grid$gamma[i], 
      lambda = hyper_grid$lambda[i], 
      alpha = hyper_grid$alpha[i]
    ) 
  )
  hyper_grid$rmse[i] <- min(m$evaluation_log$test_rmse_mean)
  
  # Safe assignment for trees
  if (is.null(m$best_iteration)) {
    hyper_grid$trees[i] <- nrow(m$evaluation_log)
  } else {
    hyper_grid$trees[i] <- m$best_iteration
  }
}

# results
hyper_grid %>%
  filter(rmse > 0) %>%
  arrange(rmse) %>%
  glimpse() # No improvement!


# Final Model
params <- list(
    objective = "reg:squarederror",
    eta = 0.01, # from I.E. 1
    max_depth = 5, # from I.E. 1
    min_child_weight = 3, # from I.E. 1
    subsample = 0.75, # from I.E. 1
    colsample_bytree = 1.0, # from I.E. 1
    colsample_bylevel = 0.5, # from I.E. 1
  verbose = 0)


# train final model
xgb.fit.final <- xgb.train(
  params = params,
  data = dtrain,
  nrounds = 471, # from last step
  verbose = 0
)



## Testing ##

xgb_recipe <- recipe(Petal.Length ~ ., data = iris_train) %>%
  step_integer(all_nominal())

xgb_prep <- prep(xgb_recipe)

train_processed <- bake(xgb_prep, iris_train)
test_processed  <- bake(xgb_prep, iris_test)

X_test <- as.matrix(test_processed[setdiff(names(test_processed), "Petal.Length")])
dtest <- xgb.DMatrix(X_test)

pred <- predict(xgb.fit.final, dtest)

library(caret)
postResample(pred, test_processed$Petal.Length)
```
